channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Declines to near 1.3250 as bearish bias persists below 100-day moving average
item.description: The GBP/USD pair trades in negative territory around 1.3250 during the early European trading hours on Thursday. The British Pound (GBP) edges lower against the US Dollar (USD) amid widening monetary policy divergence between the Bank of England (BoE) and the US Federal Reserve (Fed).

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: On verge of 78.6% Fibo breakdown near 0.6950
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) is up against its major currency pairs on Thursday, but is almost flat against the US Dollar (USD) at around 0.6948 in the early European trade.

item.title: Swiss Franc reaches fresh 16-month lows ahead of CPI data
item.description: USD/CHF continues its winning streak for the seventh consecutive trading day, reaching its fresh 16-month high of 0.8367 during Asian hours on Thursday. The currency pair appreciated as the Swiss Franc (CHF) lost ground due to sharply weakening investor sentiment in September.

item.title: Indian Rupee falls as US Treasury Yields hit fresh two-decade high near 5.3%
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) weakens against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday after an upside move the previous day. The Indian currency faces selling pressure as United States (US) Treasury Yields extend their rally, supporting the USD/INR pair to move higher to near 95.93.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Bears await acceptance below $88.00, 50% Fibo. support breakdown
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US Crude Oil price – comes under some renewed selling pressure during the Asian session on Thursday, reversing the previous day's modest recovery gains.

item.title: AUD/JPY Price Forecast: Recovers from six-month low, but retains bearish bias below 100-day SMA
item.description: The AUD/JPY cross trades in positive territory around 109.95 during the early European session on Thursday.

item.title: Gold bulls seem hesitant as resilient US Dollar and yields cap upside
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) attracts some dip-buyers near the $4,139 region during the Asian session on Thursday, stalling the previous day's pullback from the $4,220 area, touched in reaction to softer-than-expected US inflation data.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Tests nine-day EMA barrier after rebounding above 179.00
item.description: EUR/JPY halts its four-day losing streak, trading around 179.20 during Asian hours on Thursday. Technical analysis of the daily chart shows that the currency cross remains confined within a descending channel pattern. This continuous formation reinforces a persistent bearish outlook for the pair.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices rose in India on Thursday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: United States Dollar Index approaches yearly high near 101.80, US ISM PMI in focus
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) outperforms its major currency peers on Thursday. In the Asian session, the US Dollar Index (DXY), which gauges the Greenback’s value against six major currencies, trades 0.13% higher to near 101.60. The DXY is little far from its yearly high of 101.80.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD holds above $61.00 amid easing Fed rate hike expectations
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) gains ground after posting losses the previous day, trading around $60.90 per troy ounce during Asian hours on Thursday.

item.title: Japanese Yen drops to weekly low as elevated US bond yields lift USD to two-month high
item.description: The USD/JPY pair builds on the previous day's bounce from the 156.40-156.35 region, or a one-and-a-half-week low, and gains strong follow-through traction during the Asian session on Thursday.

item.title: Euro weakens below 1.1350 on higher US Treasury yields, Lagarde's dovish tilt
item.description: The EUR/USD pair drifts lower to around 1.1325 during the early Asian trading hours on Thursday. The US Dollar (USD) strengthens against the Euro (EUR) amid an extended rise in US Treasury yields. The US weekly Initial Jobless Claims report and the Fedspeak will be the highlights later in the day.

item.title: Fed path shaped by firm inflation – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Jan Groen reviews August US inflation and growth data, highlighting that Core PCE came in softer than expected but underlying price pressures in services remain firm. Benchmark revisions lowered measured inflation but still show it above levels consistent with the Federal Reserve’s target. Stronger consumption and GDP revisions suggest the US economy entered 2H26 with more momentum, keeping an October rate hike possible.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed outlook supported by robust data – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists Oscar Munoz and Eli Nir assess US PCE and GDP revisions as broadly supportive for a firm US macro backdrop and a still-hawkish Federal Reserve stance. They highlight robust US growth, sticky inflation and upgraded GDP forecasts, arguing that lower inflation revisions do not materially alter the narrative for the US Dollar or Fed policy expectations.

item.title: Australian Dollar remains stronger against Japanese Yen following Trade Balance data
item.description: AUD/JPY halts its seven-day losing streak, trading around 109.80 during Asian hours on Thursday. The currency cross remains stronger as the Australian Dollar (AUD) holds gains following the release of domestic Trade Balance data.

item.title: British Pound retreats further from one-week top as USD buying remains unabated
item.description: The GBP/USD pair edges lower during the Asian session on Thursday, retreating further from levels beyond the 1.3300 mark, or a one-week high, touched the previous day.

item.title: Australian Dollar declines below 0.6959 as Trade Surplus shrinks sharply
item.description: The AUD/USD pair trades with mild losses around 0.6945 during the early Asian session on Thursday. The Australian Dollar (AUD) edges lower against the US Dollar (USD) following Australia's Trade Balance data.

item.title: Reserve Bank of Australia: Households, businesses can weather slower economy, falling house prices
item.description: In its Financial Stability Review (FSR) published on Thursday, the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) said that “households and businesses are well placed to weather a slower economy and falling house prices.”

item.title: AUD495M: Australia’s Trade Surplus shrinks sharply in August
item.description: Australia's Trade Balance narrowed to A$495M MoM in August, followed a surplus of A$1,351M in the previous reading (revised from A$1,923M), according to the latest foreign trade data published by the Australian Bureau of Statistics on Thursday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar seems vulnerable near two-month low as USD maintains bullish undertone
item.description: The USD/CAD pair holds steady around the 1.4235 area during the Asian session on Thursday, consolidating its recent strong gains registered over the past four weeks or so.

item.title: US President Donald Trump announces $200 billion South Korean investment in US nuclear
item.description: US President Donald Trump unveiled a $200 billion investment plan from South Korea, $54 billion of which is slated to go to a liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Alaska, Reuters reported on Thursday.

item.title: WTI falls to near $89.00 as Middle East oil shipments recover
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price loses ground after posting modest gains in the previous day, trading around $89.10 per barrel during Asian hours on Thursday.

item.title: US Secretary Rubio orders Iranian delegation to leave the country
item.description: The US official stated on Monday that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told the Iranian delegation to the United Nations General Assembly immediately leave the United States (US) after talks stalled, Axios reported.

item.title: BoJ Summary of Opinions: Member says appropriate to keep raising rates in line with economy, price
item.description: The Bank of Japan (BoJ) published the Summary of Opinions from the September monetary policy meeting, with the key findings noted below.

item.title: The Japanese Yen spikes on softer US inflation and gives the gain back
item.description: Softer US inflation pulled October Fed hike odds down to near 35%, and USD/JPY fell below 156.50 on the release. It finished back just under 157.50, its fourth straight close on the 157.00 handle. The Yen got the US number it needed and USD/JPY still closed a touch above where it opened.

item.title: Japan’s Tankan Large Manufacturing Index rises to 24 in Q3 vs. 25 expected
item.description: The Bank of Japan’s (BoJ) Tankan survey of business sentiment improved slightly but missed market forecasts in the manufacturing sector. Japan’s Tankan Large Manufacturing Index rose to 24 in the third quarter (Q3) from 22 in the previous reading, weaker than the market expectation of 25.

item.title: The New Zealand Dollar edges lower as US yields outweigh China's beats
item.description: The Kiwi has followed US bond yields all month, and better numbers from New Zealand's biggest export market didn't change that on Wednesday. China's official services index came in at 50.2 against a 49.3 forecast, and the private services and factory gauges beat as well.

item.title: The Euro slips as Europe's biggest economies report hotter inflation
item.description: Germany, France, Italy and Spain all reported September inflation above forecast, which should have lifted bets on another European Central Bank (ECB) hike and the Euro with them. EUR/USD closed lower instead, its second straight close under 1.1350.

item.title: Gold falls to near $4,150 as higher Treasury yields, oil prices outweigh softer PCE inflation
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) tumbles to near $4,150 during the early Asian session on Thursday, pressured by elevated US Treasury bond yields. Traders await the US September employment data for fresh impetus, which will be released later on Friday.
